title: How to start an instant Zoom meeting on Mac: desktop steps for Zoom Workplace
metaTitle: How to start an instant Zoom meeting on Mac: step by step
description: How to start an instant Zoom meeting on Mac: open Home in the Zoom desktop app, click New Meeting, then invite people. Steps for macOS 10.15 and later.

intro: To start an instant Zoom meeting on Mac, open the Zoom desktop app, click the Home tab, then click the New Meeting icon. The meeting starts right away, and nobody is invited until you send them an invite.
tldr: Open the Zoom desktop app, sign in, and click Home in the navigation menu.
Click the New Meeting icon. The meeting starts at once with its own meeting ID.
Use the down arrow beside New Meeting to start with video or to use your personal meeting ID.
Nobody is invited by default, so send the invite yourself after the meeting opens.
Zoom's help pages list no Mac keyboard shortcut for this, so use the mouse or trackpad.

blocks.text: An instant meeting starts now. You do not pick a date, a time, or a calendar slot. Zoom calls this an instant meeting, and the steps below cover the Zoom desktop app first, because most people start calls there. Two shorter routes come after that: the Zoom Chat tab and a browser.
Start an instant meeting from the Zoom desktop app

Open the Zoom app from Applications or the Dock, then sign in with your Zoom account. If your app shows the name Zoom Workplace, that is the desktop app Zoom's help pages describe. Click Home in the navigation menu. The New Meeting icon sits on the Home tab.

Click the New Meeting icon. The meeting window opens, and you are the host. Zoom's instant-meeting article says nobody is invited by default, so the room stays empty until you bring people in. The meeting ID expires as soon as the meeting ends, so do not plan to reuse it.
Choose video on or off before you start

Next to the New Meeting icon is a small down arrow. Click it to see two options. Start with video opens the meeting with your camera on. Use my personal meeting ID (PMI) starts the meeting with your PMI, the fixed number tied to your account, instead of a new ID.

blocks.text: Use the plain New Meeting icon for a one-off call. Use your PMI for a group that meets on the same link every time. If you are not sure, start with the plain icon. You can always send the meeting ID to people after the call opens.
Invite people to an instant meeting

Nobody joins an instant meeting unless you invite them, and Zoom's article says so directly. Once the meeting window is open, look for the invite option in the meeting controls. Send the invite link or meeting ID right away, so people can join when they are ready.

Older guides describe a different path. Macworld's Zoom for Mac guide, dated May 5, 2020, says to click Participants in the meeting controls, then Invite. That guide is old, and Zoom's current interface may use different labels. Treat that path as a hint and look for the word Invite.
Start an instant meeting from the Zoom Chat tab

Zoom also starts meetings from chat. Open the Zoom Chat tab, select a contact or a channel name, then click the video camera icon. The meeting invites every member of that group chat or channel. Check the member list first, because a large channel sends a large invite.

A worked example helps. Suppose your whole department sits in one channel, and you need a quick word with one colleague. Starting the call from that channel calls everyone in it. Open a group chat with only the people you need, then start the call there. Nobody else gets pulled in.
Start an instant meeting in a browser

Type zoom.new in your browser's address bar, and Zoom starts an instant meeting. Zoom says this works in a browser, and account owner and admin settings still apply. If your company limits instant meetings, the link may not work for you, so ask your admin.

You can also use the Zoom Web App. Sign in, click New Meeting, and let the browser run the call. When the prompts appear, click Allow for the microphone first, then the camera. Zoom says microphone access is required, or people will not hear you.
Give your browser microphone and camera access

If the browser never asked, or you blocked the request earlier, open the Apple menu, then System Settings, then Privacy & Security. Under Microphone and Camera, tick your browser. Zoom lists Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge. Tick the one you use.

Screen sharing has its own switch. Open Screen & System Audio Recording in the same Privacy & Security view, and tick your browser there too. Zoom lists it as a separate step, so do not skip it if you plan to share your screen.

Zoom's article says macOS Mojave 10.14 or later requires microphone access for the browser. On a current Mac, that step is required, not optional. Check those prompts before a call that matters, because a blocked microphone stays silent until you change its setting.
Check your macOS version before you click New Meeting

Zoom's system requirements list macOS 10.15 or later for the desktop app, with a dual-core 2GHz processor as the minimum. If your Mac runs an older system, Zoom says version 6.7.7 is the last Zoom Workplace app for macOS below 10.15. Starting with 7.0.0, the app dropped support for macOS 10.13 and 10.14.

Check your app version before you start. Menus shift between releases, and the Home tab may look different after a redesign. Zoom's What's New page lists October 2026 changes, including a simplified Workplace interface. That page lists no Mac-specific change to starting a meeting, but check the release notes for your build.
Find your app version inside the Zoom app, then compare it with the requirements page. If an update prompt appears, follow the update guide before you troubleshoot anything else.
Free plan limits to know before you start
The Basic plan gives you 40 minutes per meeting and up to 100 participants. Zoom's pricing page lists both limits. Zoom's free video conferencing page says you can upgrade to meet for up to 30 hours.

Say you start a quick check-in and the talk runs long. The 40-minute limit applies to that meeting, not to your account as a whole. Decide before you start whether the topic fits in that time. If it does not, plan a longer call or a paid plan.
Mistakes people make with instant meetings

items: Sharing the link after the call. Instant meeting IDs expire when the meeting ends, so the old link stops working.
Assuming someone is waiting. Nobody is invited by default, so the room can stay empty.
Skipping microphone access in a browser. Zoom says people will not hear you without it.
Starting from a large channel. The Zoom Chat route invites every member of that group.
Using the PMI for everything. A fixed meeting ID suits a regular group, but a one-off call does not need it.

blocks.text: When the New Meeting button does nothing

The official pages do not cover every error. Update prompts, installation errors and Full Disk Access problems show up in community forums, and this guide does not list fixes for them. Start with the basics: sign out, sign in again, and update the app. For the update steps, see [how to update Zoom on Mac](/how-to/update-zoom-in-zoom).

If the meeting starts but nobody sees your screen, read [how to fix a black screen share in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/fix-a-black-screen-share-in-zoom). For camera problems, read [how to grant camera access in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/grant-camera-access-in-zoom).
Instant meeting or scheduled meeting: which one fits

An instant meeting suits a call that starts now. If you need a fixed time or a calendar invite, schedule the meeting instead. The steps are in [how to schedule a Zoom meeting on Mac](/how-to/schedule-a-meeting-in-zoom). If someone else sent you a link, follow [how to join a Zoom meeting on Mac](/how-to/join-a-meeting-in-zoom) instead of starting your own.
Set up your Mac before the first call

Test your microphone and camera before the first call of the day. Sit where the Mac can see you, and check that the sound comes from the device you expect. Close other apps that use the camera, because a second app can keep it busy.
Check which device is set for audio. If you use headphones, plug them in before you start. Starting a meeting on the wrong speaker is a common slip, and it takes seconds to fix before the call opens.
What to do once the meeting is running

Mute yourself when you are not talking, especially in a room with background noise. The steps are in [how to mute yourself in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/mute-yourself-in-zoom). When you need to show a document or a window, [how to share screen in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/share-your-screen-in-zoom) covers the desktop steps and the shortcuts.
Once the meeting ends, its ID expires. Start a new instant meeting for the next call, and send the new invite from there.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to start an instant Zoom meeting on Mac?
faq.answer: Zoom's instant-meeting article does not list a keyboard shortcut for starting a meeting on Mac. Use the mouse or trackpad to click the New Meeting icon on the Home tab.

faq.question: Why does nobody join my instant meeting?
faq.answer: Nobody is invited by default, so the room can start empty. Send the invite link or meeting ID yourself, and check that the people you invited have it.

faq.question: Can I reuse the link from an instant meeting?
faq.answer: No. Zoom says instant meeting IDs from the desktop or mobile app expire immediately after the meeting ends. Start a new instant meeting for the next call.

faq.question: Does zoom.new work in every browser?
faq.answer: Zoom says typing zoom.new in a browser address bar starts an instant meeting, and account owner and admin settings still apply. Zoom's Mac permission steps name Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge.

faq.question: Do I need the desktop app to start an instant meeting?
faq.answer: No. You can use the Zoom Web App in a browser or the zoom.new address. The Web App needs microphone and camera permission, because Zoom says people will not hear you without microphone access.

faq.question: Which macOS version does the Zoom desktop app need?
faq.answer: Zoom's system requirements list macOS 10.15 or later for the desktop app. Zoom says Workplace app 6.7.7 is the last version for macOS below 10.15, so check the requirements page before you update.

faq.question: What is the free plan limit for an instant meeting?
faq.answer: The Basic plan allows 40 minutes per meeting and up to 100 participants. Zoom's pricing page lists both limits, so check it before a long call.

steps.name: Open Zoom and sign in
steps.text: Open the Zoom app from Applications or the Dock, then sign in with your Zoom account. If the app shows the name Zoom Workplace, it is the same desktop app.

steps.name: Click Home
steps.text: In the navigation menu, click the Home tab. The New Meeting icon sits on this tab.

steps.name: Optional: pick a start option
steps.text: Click the down arrow beside the New Meeting icon. Choose Start with video to open with your camera on, or Use my personal meeting ID (PMI) to start with your PMI.

steps.name: Click New Meeting
steps.text: Click the New Meeting icon. The meeting window opens, and you are the host.

steps.name: Allow microphone and camera
steps.text: If macOS asks for microphone or camera access, allow it. Zoom says microphone access is required, or people will not hear you.

steps.name: Invite people
steps.text: Nobody is invited by default. Use the invite option in the meeting controls, then send the invite link or meeting ID. Look for the word Invite, since the label can change between versions.

troubleshooting.problem: The New Meeting button does nothing
troubleshooting.fix: Sign out, sign in again, and update the Zoom app. Zoom's pages I could open do not list fixes for every error, so use the update guide if a prompt appears.
Open Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone, then tick your browser or the Zoom app. Zoom says microphone access is required.
Open Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera, then tick your browser or the Zoom app. Close other apps that may use the camera.
Open Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, tick your browser or the Zoom app, then start the share again.

troubleshooting.problem: The old meeting link stops working
troubleshooting.fix: Instant meeting IDs expire when the meeting ends. Start a new instant meeting, or schedule one if the call must happen later.
